searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — chesed brainstorm: make every mobile surface inviting the awtsmoos creates the reader, the tree, the composer, and the social road anew; awtsmoos.com should greet the thumb with one clear deed, while deeper instruments wait for the user to choose. screenshot wounds that must become durable contracts the heichel/post reader can render raw server exception text instead of torah content. heichel tree cards consume too much vertical space and expose advanced platform controls over content. social composer overlays a large review/publish command slab over the writing canvas. composer shows too many format/media/creator detail choices simultaneously on a narrow phone. social hub production still shows the old expanded identity/context stack and large discovery controls. the advanced tool affordance can overlap meaningful content. multiple mobile docks use different spacing, elevation, labels, and interruption patterns. blank/fallback/loading states are not consistently inviting or actionable. twenty possible improvements 1. repair dynamic reader template composition before styling. 2. add a reader template regression test that executes the real composition contract. 3. render a calm reader recovery state instead of raw stack traces if data fails. 4. make the reader content itself the first visible surface. 5. collapse reader utilities behind one compact tools disclosure. 6. keep reading controls below or beside content rather than over it. 7. reduce heichel series card vertical padding and metadata chrome. 8. keep one primary card action visible and move secondary actions into overflow. 9. make platform/advanced tools a true closed disclosure on mobile. 10. prevent advanced panels from floating over the bottom dock. 11. preserve current heichel mobile first work rather than overwrite it. 12. make composer identity a compact row, not a large card. 13. make post/photo/video mode selection a compact segmented control. 14. put advanced media formats behind one disclosure. 15. put creator details behind one disclosure. 16. replace the giant sticky publish slab with a compact bottom action bar. 17. ensure the bottom action bar never covers editable content. 18. share mobile safe area and dock clearance tokens across surfaces where practical. 19. keep motion/glass subtle and never animate blur. 20. verify every affected route at 390px and 320px with real chrome. the awtsmoos is not hidden by simplicity; simplicity removes the false walls that hide the deed.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — gevurah critique: bound the repair by real ownership the awtsmoos gives every ohr a keli and every possibility a border; awtsmoos.com must improve the lived road without trampling concurrent work or inventing a new order. known boundaries shared checkout contains unrelated dirty work and active heichel edits. whole file rewrites only; translate them into bounded user facing recovery. 4. keep reader apis and url contracts stable. 5. inspect existing reader tests before adding a new test. 6. inspect heichel dirty diff before touching any overlapping file. 7. prefer a clean worktree for new cross page changes when overlap is risky. 8. if current heichel edits are good, preserve them as observed candidate work rather than recreate them. 9. never stage unrelated repository changes. 10. keep primary navigation reachable with one thumb. 11. keep bottom bars below content and include safe area clearance. 12. avoid position: fixed for large multi row controls on phones. 13. allow only compact single row fixed actions when truly persistent. 14. do not hide essential publishing validation behind advanced disclosures. 15. keep form labels and errors visible when fields are active. 16. preserve keyboard navigation and native details semantics. 17. preserve reduced motion and reduced transparency behavior. 18. test fallback/loading/error states, not only happy paths. 19. verify actual production source signatures after deployment. 20. keep remaining work open until reader, tree, composer, hub, and deployment are proven. gevurah does not choke the light; it shapes the glass so the light can be read.
